Let
\[
\sqrt{n^2+3n+1}=\sqrt{(n+1)^2+n}=(n+1)\sqrt{1+\frac{n}{(n+1)^2}}.
\]
Since \(n>100\), \(\frac{n}{(n+1)^2}<\frac1{n+1}\), so the decimal part is
\[
f=\sqrt{n^2+3n+1}-(n+1)
=\frac{n}{2(n+1)}-\frac{n^2}{8(n+1)^3}+\cdots
\]
For \(n>100\),
\[
f<\frac{n}{2(n+1)}<\frac12,
\]
and
\[
f>\frac{n}{2(n+1)}-\frac{n^2}{8(n+1)^3}
> \frac{101}{204}-\frac1{808}>0.49.
\]
Thus \(0.49<f<0.50\), so the first two digits of the decimal part are \(49\).

\[
\boxed{49}
\]
